Population increased in Swindon

The estimated population of Swindon in 2024 was 243,875 usual residents, a rise of 1.5% since 2023.

This meant that Swindon's rate of population change placed it about average among local authority districts in England and Wales.

In the period from mid-2021 to mid-2024, the population estimate of Swindon increased by 4.3%.

Over this slightly longer period, Swindon was also among the areas that had a broadly average population increase, of local authority districts in England and Wales.

Age profile of Swindon

The average (median) age stayed at 39.8 years between 2023 and 2024.

You can see how the age profile of Swindon has changed since 2011 in the population pyramid below.

sections.content:
Swindon is an area that is classed as urban in nature according to the 2021 Census Rural Urban Classification.

By age category, Swindon's population of 243,875 usual residents was made up of:

  • 48,180 people aged 0 to 15 years, (19.8%)
  • 155,927 people aged 16 to 64 years, (63.9%)
  • 39,768 people aged 65 years and over, (16.3%)

    • Compared with England and Wales as a whole, Swindon has a slightly lower proportion of people aged 65 years and over (16.3% compared with 18.9% for England and Wales).

Contributors to population change

We look at different flows of people into and out of areas and births and deaths to see what is driving population change in each area.

In Swindon, the largest contribution to population change in the year to mid-2024 was from net international migration.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Swindon
sections.subtitle: How the population changed, by component

sections.content:
We estimate that, for Swindon, between 2023 and 2024:

  • More births than deaths increased the population of 480 people (0.2%). In total, there were 2,391 births and 1,911 deaths in Swindon.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other areas in the UK) led to a fall in the population of 166 (-0.1%). There were 9,566 people entering the area and 9,732 people leaving the area.
  • Net international migration led to an increase in Swindon's population of 3,247 (1.4%) as a result of 4,416 people entering the area and 1,169 people leaving the area.
  • Other change (which includes changes to armed forces personnel and prisoners) for Swindon was less than 0.1%.

Revisions to 2023 population estimates

We regularly revise our initial population estimates as we get more data and methods improve.

Our revised estimate for the population of Swindon in mid-2023 is 240,218.

Within this, international migration was revised upwards by 1,889 people and internal migration estimates were revised downwards by 88 people.

Overall, there was an revision upwards of 1,801 people.
